title: Active-Attack Detection for Group Key Progression
summary: Preventing active attacks in Group Key Progression is challenging; whether two-party detection mechanisms extend to group protocols remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether active-attack detection mechanisms for two-party messaging can be extended to Group Key Progression (GKP) protocols for groups, given that preventing active attacks is challenging and detecting them may instead be an acceptable goal.

scope.domain: Active-attack detection for Group Key Progression protocols in group messaging.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether active-attack detection mechanisms developed for two-party messaging can be extended to Group Key Progression protocols for groups.

citations.label: Group Key Progression: Strong Security for Shared Persistent Data

progress.summary: The source describes preventing active attacks as challenging and suggests detection as an acceptable practical goal. It presents extending two-party detection mechanisms to groups as a promising direction.
citation_labels: Matilda Backendal et al., Group Key Progression: Strong Security for Shared Persistent Data
